results.structuredChinese: 我挺喜欢喝咖啡的，主要是因为早上经常比较困，喝一杯会让我清醒一点。现在这已经成了我的日常习惯，不过我通常一天只喝一杯。
results.spokenEnglish: I quite like coffee, mainly because I'm usually pretty tired in the morning, and a cup helps me wake up a bit. It's become part of my daily routine now, though I normally just stick to one cup a day.

results.structuredChinese: 我挺喜欢喝咖啡的，主要是因为早上经常比较困，喝一杯会让我清醒一点。现在这已经成了我的日常习惯，不过我通常一天只喝一杯。
results.spokenEnglish: I do enjoy coffee, mainly because I tend to feel pretty groggy in the mornings, and a cup really helps me wake up a bit. It's become part of my daily routine now, though I usually stick to just one cup a day.

results.structuredChinese: 我挺喜欢喝咖啡的，主要是因为早上经常比较困，喝一杯会让我清醒一点。现在这已经成了我的日常习惯，不过我通常一天只喝一杯。
results.spokenEnglish: I do enjoy coffee, mainly because I tend to feel pretty groggy in the mornings, and a cup really helps me wake up a bit. It's become part of my daily routine now, though I usually stick to just one cup a day.

results.structuredChinese: 周末我基本就是宅在家里，累了一周真的不想折腾。大部分时间就刷刷剧，算是给自己彻底放空一下，感觉这样最舒服。
results.spokenEnglish: I mostly just stay in at the weekend, to be honest. After a long week, I really can't be bothered going out. I spend most of my time binge-watching shows, which is my way of completely switching off. That's when I feel most relaxed.

results.structuredChinese: 我更喜欢住在大城市，主要是因为生活方便，工作机会也多。不过人确实太多了，有时候会觉得有点吵，尤其是上下班高峰期。
results.spokenEnglish: I definitely prefer living in a big city — mainly because everything's so convenient and there are way more job opportunities. That said, it can get pretty overwhelming with the crowds, and it does get noisy sometimes, especially during rush hour.

results.structuredChinese: 我以前不太喜欢看书，现在偶尔会看一点。主要看当时有没有时间和心情，不会强迫自己每天都读。
results.spokenEnglish: I didn't use to enjoy reading much, but I pick up a book every now and then these days. It really depends on whether I've got the time and I'm in the right mood — I don't force myself to read every day or anything like that.

results.structuredChinese: 我想说家里找到的一台旧相机。它不贵，外表也很普通，但拍出来的颜色偏暖，跟手机照片很不一样。带它出门有点麻烦，拍完也不能马上看到效果，不过我还是很喜欢。它会让我拍照时慢下来，更认真地观察眼前的东西，所以对我来说挺特别的。
results.spokenEnglish: I'd like to talk about an old camera I found at home. It wasn't expensive, and it looks pretty ordinary from the outside, but the colours come out warm and slightly faded, which is completely different from phone photos. Taking it out is a bit of a hassle, and you can't check the results straight away, but I still really like using it. It forces me to slow down when I'm taking pictures and pay more attention to what's actually in front of me, so it's become something quite special to me.

results.structuredChinese: 我想说家里找到的一台旧相机。它不贵，外表也很普通，但拍出来的颜色偏暖，跟手机照片很不一样。带它出门有点麻烦，拍完也不能马上看到效果，不过我还是很喜欢。它会让我拍照时慢下来，更认真地观察眼前的东西，所以对我来说挺特别的。
results.spokenEnglish: I'd like to talk about an old camera I found at home. It wasn't expensive, and it looks pretty ordinary on the outside, but the colours come out warm and slightly faded — nothing like the sharp, bright photos you get from a phone. Taking it out is a bit of a hassle, and you can't check your shots straight away, which takes some getting used to. But I still love using it. It forces me to slow down and really look at what's in front of me instead of just snapping away. That makes it feel special — almost like the camera's teaching me to pay attention again.

results.structuredChinese: 我想说家里找到的一台旧相机。它不贵，外表也很普通，但拍出来的颜色偏暖，跟手机照片很不一样。带它出门有点麻烦，拍完也不能马上看到效果，不过我还是很喜欢。它会让我拍照时慢下来，更认真地观察眼前的东西，所以对我来说挺特别的。
results.spokenEnglish: I'd like to talk about this old camera I found at home. It wasn't expensive, and honestly it looks pretty ordinary from the outside. But the colours come out really warm, which is completely different from the photos you get on a phone. It's a bit of a hassle to carry around, and you can't check the shot right after you've taken it, so there's that frustration. But I still love using it. What it does is force me to slow down when I'm taking pictures, to actually look at what's in front of me rather than just snapping away. That makes it special to me.

results.structuredChinese: 去年夏天，我跟几个好朋友去了一趟海边，那是我第一次看到海上日出。第二天我们很早起床，天还黑着就走到海边。看到太阳从海平面慢慢升起来时，我觉得早起很值得。回来的路上大家都很累，但那次经历让我明白，有时候稍微折腾一下，能换来很特别的体验。
results.spokenEnglish: Last summer I went to the seaside with a few close friends, and it was actually the first time I'd ever seen the sunrise over the ocean. The next day we got up really early — it was still pitch black when we made our way down to the beach. Watching the sun come up slowly from the horizon, I just felt that getting up so early had been completely worth it. On the way back everyone was pretty exhausted, but that whole experience made me realise something — sometimes going a bit out of your way, putting in that extra effort, can lead to something really special.

results.structuredChinese: 我想说一条旧围巾。那是几年前我刚工作时，我妈妈亲手织给我的。围巾是深灰色的，针脚不算整齐，但很厚实。后来每年冬天我都会拿出来戴，虽然边角已经起球了，我还是舍不得扔。它对我来说不只是一条围巾，更像是一种被家人惦记的感觉。
results.spokenEnglish: I'd like to talk about an old scarf of mine. My mum knitted it for me with her own hands when I'd just started working a few years back. It's a dark grey colour, and the stitches aren't exactly even, but the fabric's really thick and warm. Every winter since then, I've pulled it out and worn it, and even though the edges have gone all bobbly now, I still can't bring myself to throw it away. It's become more than just a scarf to me — it's this feeling of being looked after, of having someone in my family thinking about me.

results.structuredChinese: 我想说一位帮助过我的老师。以前我上课不太敢提问，总担心自己的问题太简单。她很耐心，从来不会因为学生答错而不耐烦，还会鼓励我慢慢说。后来我开始愿意举手，也更有信心了。我最感谢她的地方，是她让我觉得犯错并不可怕。
results.spokenEnglish: I'd like to talk about a teacher who really helped me out. I used to be quite hesitant about asking questions in class — I was always worried mine would sound too simple or even stupid. But she was incredibly patient. She never got frustrated when a student gave the wrong answer, and she'd actually encourage me to take my time and just speak at my own pace. Gradually, I started raising my hand more often, and I could feel my confidence growing bit by bit. What I'm most grateful for is that she made me feel that making mistakes wasn't something to be afraid of — and that changed everything for me.

results.structuredChinese: 我觉得政府应该发展公共交通，因为城市堵车很严重。如果公交和地铁更方便，更多人会愿意少开车，这能减少拥堵和空气污染。不过不同城市情况不同，政府还是要根据当地需求选择合适的方式。
results.spokenEnglish: I think the government should invest more in public transport, because traffic jams in cities are really serious. If buses and subways were more convenient, more people would be willing to drive less, and that would help cut down on congestion and air pollution. But different cities have different situations, so the government still needs to choose the right approach based on local needs.

results.structuredChinese: 我觉得政府应该发展公共交通，因为城市堵车很严重。如果公交和地铁更方便，更多人会愿意少开车，这能减少拥堵和空气污染。不过不同城市情况不同，政府还是要根据当地需求选择合适的方式。
results.spokenEnglish: I'd say investing in public transport is one of the most effective things governments can do, simply because traffic congestion has become such a nightmare in so many cities. If buses and subways were genuinely more convenient, I think a lot more people would actually choose to leave their cars at home, and that would obviously ease congestion and cut down on air pollution too. At the same time, it really depends on the city you're talking about — what works in one place might not suit another — so governments still need to look at local conditions and figure out the most practical approach for each area.

results.structuredChinese: 我觉得政府应该发展公共交通，因为城市堵车很严重。如果公交和地铁更方便，更多人会愿意少开车，这能减少拥堵和空气污染。不过不同城市情况不同，政府还是要根据当地需求选择合适的方式。
results.spokenEnglish: I'd say investing in public transport is one of the most effective things governments can do, simply because traffic congestion has become such a nightmare in so many cities. If buses and subways were genuinely more convenient — more frequent, better connected, more reliable — I think a lot of people would actually choose to leave their cars at home. That shift would ease congestion and cut air pollution at the same time. At the same time, it really depends on the city. What works in a dense metropolis might not suit a sprawling place with lower population, so governments still need to tailor their approach to local conditions rather than applying the same formula everywhere.

results.structuredChinese: 我觉得远程工作确实方便，不用每天通勤，时间也更自由。但沟通会比较麻烦，比如线上等回复可能很久，有些复杂的事情只靠文字或视频也容易产生误解。所以它有明显好处，但公司需要找到改善沟通的方法。
results.spokenEnglish: Remote working is definitely convenient — you don't have to commute every day, and you've got more freedom with your time. But communication can be tricky. Waiting for replies online can take ages, and some complicated things are easy to misunderstand when you're only using text or video calls. So there are clear benefits, but companies really need to find ways to improve how people stay in touch.

results.structuredChinese: 我觉得学校只教考试内容肯定不够，因为学生以后还需要工作、沟通和合作。不过基础知识也不能丢，它是学习其他能力的底子。关键是平衡，例如设计得好的小组任务可以同时训练知识运用和团队协作，但如果只是少数人完成全部工作，就没有意义。
results.spokenEnglish: I think schools that only teach what's on the exam are definitely selling students short, because later on they'll need to hold down a job, communicate effectively and work with other people. That said, you can't just ditch the fundamentals either — they're the building blocks for everything else. What it really comes down to is getting the balance right. A well-designed group project, for instance, can get students applying what they've learned while also picking up teamwork skills. But it only works if everyone's actually pulling their weight — if it's just one or two people doing all the work, it defeats the whole purpose.

results.structuredChinese: 限制私家车可能缓解拥堵和污染，但公平性是个问题。市中心公共交通密集，限制开车比较可行；住在郊区的人可能没有可靠替代方式。政策能否奏效取决于公共交通覆盖、班次和具体限制方式，也需要平衡环境效益、通勤需求和不同收入群体承担的成本。
results.spokenEnglish: Restricting private cars could ease congestion and pollution, but fairness is a real concern. In city centres, where public transport is already dense, limiting car use is fairly workable. The problem is people in the suburbs often don't have a reliable alternative. Whether a policy actually succeeds comes down to three things: how comprehensive the public transport network is, how frequent the services are, and what form the restrictions take. There's also a balancing act between environmental gains, people's commuting needs, and the costs different income groups would have to absorb.
